fruits.extendedStory: Cangrande II della Scala began this castle in 1354. It was finished two years later, in 1356. He built it in the Gothic style, which means tall pointed arches and high walls of red brick. A bridge of the same brick runs from the castle across the river. Walk out onto Ponte Castelvecchio and you are standing on the lord's own crossing.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Cangrande II. della Scala ließ diese Burg ab 1354 bauen. Zwei Jahre später, 1356, war sie fertig. Er baute im gotischen Stil. Das bedeutet hohe Spitzbogen und hohe Mauern aus rotem Backstein. Eine Brücke aus demselben Backstein führt von der Burg über den Fluss. Wer heute über den Ponte Castelvecchio geht, geht über den Übergang des Stadtherrn.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Cangrande II della Scala began this castle in 1354. It was finished two years later, in 1356. He built it in the Gothic style, which means tall pointed arches and high walls of red brick. A bridge of the same brick runs from the castle across the river. Walk out onto Ponte Castelvecchio and you are standing on the lord's own crossing.

localizedStory.de: Eine Burg aus rotem Backstein mit eigener Brücke, dem Ponte Castelvecchio. Cangrande II. della Scala begann 1354 mit dem Bau.
localizedStory.en: A castle of red brick with its own bridge, Ponte Castelvecchio. Cangrande II della Scala began building it in 1354.

fruits.name: Castelvecchio
fruits.story: A castle of red brick with its own bridge, Ponte Castelvecchio. Cangrande II della Scala began building it in 1354.

fruits.extendedStory: The Romans built this ring around the middle of the 1st century AD, and it still stands 31 metres high. Under Theodoric, who ruled from 493 to 526, the outer wall that formed its facade was partly pulled down. Its stone went into the city's second ring of walls, and one short piece was left standing. Veronese call that piece the Ala, the wing. On 10 August 1913 Verdi's Aida rang out between these stones, and opera has been sung here ever since.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Römer bauten diesen Ring um die Mitte des 1. Jahrhunderts nach Christus, und er ist noch heute 31 Meter hoch. Unter Theoderich, der von 493 bis 526 herrschte, wurde die äußere Mauer der Fassade zum Teil abgetragen. Ihre Steine wanderten in den zweiten Mauerring der Stadt, und ein kurzes Stück blieb stehen. Die Veroneser nennen dieses Stück Ala, den Flügel. Am 10. August 1913 erklang hier Verdis Aida, und seither wird in der Arena Oper gesungen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The Romans built this ring around the middle of the 1st century AD, and it still stands 31 metres high. Under Theodoric, who ruled from 493 to 526, the outer wall that formed its facade was partly pulled down. Its stone went into the city's second ring of walls, and one short piece was left standing. Veronese call that piece the Ala, the wing. On 10 August 1913 Verdi's Aida rang out between these stones, and opera has been sung here ever since.

localizedStory.de: Das römische Amphitheater am Platz, 31 Meter hoch. Seit dem 10. August 1913 erklingt hier Oper, damals Verdis Aida.
localizedStory.en: The Roman amphitheatre on the square, 31 metres high. Since 10 August 1913 opera has filled it, starting with Verdi's Aida.

fruits.name: Arena di Verona
fruits.story: The Roman amphitheatre on the square, 31 metres high. Since 10 August 1913 opera has filled it, starting with Verdi's Aida.

fruits.extendedStory: The church goes back to 1100, so it has stood here for more than nine centuries. It carries the names of two men, Firmus and Rusticus. Inside, the decoration is Italian Baroque. That style likes curves, colour and gold, and it was added long after the walls went up. So the building is really two ages at once: plain old stone, dressed in later splendour.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Kirche geht auf das Jahr 1100 zurück und steht damit seit über neun Jahrhunderten hier. Sie trägt die Namen zweier Männer, Firmus und Rusticus. Drinnen ist die Ausstattung italienischer Barock. Dieser Stil mag Schwünge, Farbe und Gold, und er kam lange nach den Mauern dazu. So ist das Haus zugleich aus zwei Zeiten: alter schlichter Stein, später prächtig geschmückt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The church goes back to 1100, so it has stood here for more than nine centuries. It carries the names of two men, Firmus and Rusticus. Inside, the decoration is Italian Baroque. That style likes curves, colour and gold, and it was added long after the walls went up. So the building is really two ages at once: plain old stone, dressed in later splendour.

localizedStory.de: Eine Kirche, begonnen im Jahr 1100, benannt nach Firmus und Rusticus. Die spätere Ausstattung ist barock, ein Stil voller Schwünge und Gold.
localizedStory.en: A church begun in 1100, named for Firmus and Rusticus. Its later decoration is Baroque, a style full of curves and gold.

fruits.name: Chiesa di San Fermo Maggiore
fruits.story: A church begun in 1100, named for Firmus and Rusticus. Its later decoration is Baroque, a style full of curves and gold.

fruits.extendedStory: The Romans put up this gate in the 1st century AD, and you walk through it on Corso Porta Borsari. They called it Porta Iovia, after a temple to Jupiter Lustralis that stood nearby. The name it carries now is about money. Bursarii were the guards with the purse, and they collected the bishop's tolls from everyone coming in. So the gate has spent much of its life as a checkpoint.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Römer setzten dieses Tor im 1. Jahrhundert nach Christus, und heute geht man am Corso Porta Borsari hindurch. Sie nannten es Porta Iovia, nach einem Tempel für Jupiter Lustralis in der Nähe. Der heutige Name handelt vom Geld. Die Bursarii waren die Wächter mit dem Beutel, und sie kassierten den bischöflichen Zoll von allen, die hereinkamen. So war das Tor einen großen Teil seines Lebens eine Kontrollstelle.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The Romans put up this gate in the 1st century AD, and you walk through it on Corso Porta Borsari. They called it Porta Iovia, after a temple to Jupiter Lustralis that stood nearby. The name it carries now is about money. Bursarii were the guards with the purse, and they collected the bishop's tolls from everyone coming in. So the gate has spent much of its life as a checkpoint.

localizedStory.de: Ein römisches Tor aus dem 1. Jahrhundert, mitten in der Straße. Der Name kommt von den Bursarii, den Wächtern, die mit dem Beutel Zoll kassierten.
localizedStory.en: A Roman gate from the 1st century, standing in the street. Its name comes from the Bursarii, the guards who collected tolls with a purse.

fruits.name: Porta Borsari
fruits.story: A Roman gate from the 1st century, standing in the street. Its name comes from the Bursarii, the guards who collected tolls with a purse.

fruits.extendedStory: This square stands on the ground of the Roman forum, where the city did its business. Rulers used the spot to read proclamations out to the citizens. Carved into the base of that same stone are medieval units of measure. The fountain nearby is built from Roman pieces: its great basin, and its statue, which came from the Capitolium. Cansignorio della Scala had it raised to celebrate water arriving from the Lorì di Avesa stream.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Dieser Platz liegt auf dem Boden des römischen Forums, wo die Stadt ihre Geschäfte machte. Die Herrscher verlasen hier ihre Erlasse an die Bürger. In den Sockel desselben Steins sind mittelalterliche Maßeinheiten eingemeißelt. Der Brunnen daneben besteht aus römischen Teilen: sein großes Becken und seine Statue, die vom Kapitol stammt. Cansignorio della Scala ließ ihn errichten, weil endlich Wasser vom Bach Lorì di Avesa herkam.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This square stands on the ground of the Roman forum, where the city did its business. Rulers used the spot to read proclamations out to the citizens. Carved into the base of that same stone are medieval units of measure. The fountain nearby is built from Roman pieces: its great basin, and its statue, which came from the Capitolium. Cansignorio della Scala had it raised to celebrate water arriving from the Lorì di Avesa stream.

localizedStory.de: Der Marktplatz liegt auf dem römischen Forum. Schau auf den Sockel der steinernen Tribüne: Dort sind mittelalterliche Maßeinheiten eingemeißelt.
localizedStory.en: The market square sits on the old Roman forum. Look at the base of the stone tribune: medieval measuring units are carved into it.

fruits.name: Piazza delle Erbe
fruits.story: The market square sits on the old Roman forum. Look at the base of the stone tribune: medieval measuring units are carved into it.

fruits.extendedStory: The house is named for Juliet, and the city bought it in 1905, when the owners put it up for auction. The balcony that everyone photographs is not medieval. It went up in 1939 and 1940, when Antonio Avena of the civic museums had the courtyard front altered. The house opened to visitors as a museum on 1 June 1973. So the balcony people queue for is younger than their grandparents.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Haus ist nach Julia benannt, und die Stadt kaufte es 1905, als die Besitzer es versteigern ließen. Der Balkon, den alle fotografieren, ist nicht mittelalterlich. Er entstand 1939 und 1940, als Antonio Avena von den Städtischen Museen die Hoffassade umgestalten ließ. Am 1. Juni 1973 öffnete das Haus als Museum. Der Balkon ist also jünger als die Großeltern der Leute, die davor Schlange stehen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The house is named for Juliet, and the city bought it in 1905, when the owners put it up for auction. The balcony that everyone photographs is not medieval. It went up in 1939 and 1940, when Antonio Avena of the civic museums had the courtyard front altered. The house opened to visitors as a museum on 1 June 1973. So the balcony people queue for is younger than their grandparents.

localizedStory.de: Der Hof an der Via Cappello, benannt nach Julia. Sein Balkon ist jünger als gedacht: Er kam 1939, als die Wand neu gestaltet wurde.
localizedStory.en: The courtyard on Via Cappello, named for Juliet. Its balcony is younger than it looks: it went up in 1939, when the wall was rebuilt.

fruits.name: Casa di Giulietta
fruits.story: The courtyard on Via Cappello, named for Juliet. Its balcony is younger than it looks: it went up in 1939, when the wall was rebuilt.

fruits.extendedStory: Three great tombs stand here, raised between the 14th and 15th centuries for Mastino II, Cangrande I and Cansignorio della Scala. Cangrande died suddenly in 1329, during the siege of Treviso. His nephew Mastino II, who ruled from 1329 to 1351, had a grand monument built for him above the church door. So the lord lies over the way in. The family badge was a ladder, scala in Italian, and on Bartolomeo's tomb it is topped by an eagle.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Drei große Gräber stehen hier, errichtet im 14. und 15. Jahrhundert für Mastino II., Cangrande I. und Cansignorio della Scala. Cangrande starb 1329 plötzlich, während der Belagerung von Treviso. Sein Neffe Mastino II., der von 1329 bis 1351 regierte, ließ ihm ein prächtiges Grabmal über dem Kirchenportal errichten. So liegt der Herr über dem Eingang. Das Zeichen der Familie war eine Leiter, auf Italienisch scala, und auf dem Grab des Bartolomeo krönt sie ein Adler.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Three great tombs stand here, raised between the 14th and 15th centuries for Mastino II, Cangrande I and Cansignorio della Scala. Cangrande died suddenly in 1329, during the siege of Treviso. His nephew Mastino II, who ruled from 1329 to 1351, had a grand monument built for him above the church door. So the lord lies over the way in. The family badge was a ladder, scala in Italian, and on Bartolomeo's tomb it is topped by an eagle.

localizedStory.de: Steinerne Gräber der Herren von Verona hinter einem Eisengitter. Achte auf die Leiter im Gitter: Die scala war das Zeichen der Familie.
localizedStory.en: Stone tombs of Verona's lords behind an iron fence. Look for the ladder in the ironwork: scala was the family's own badge.

fruits.name: Arche Scaligere
fruits.story: Stone tombs of Verona's lords behind an iron fence. Look for the ladder in the ironwork: scala was the family's own badge.

fruits.extendedStory: Work began here in 1290, and the church was still going up in 1471. That is nearly two centuries of building, and families lived beside the site for generations. The masons who began it never saw the roof. It is Gothic, a style that reaches upward, and it stands 72 metres from the ground to the tip. The church is named for Anastasia of Rome.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Bau begann 1290, und 1471 wurde immer noch daran gearbeitet. Das sind fast zwei Jahrhunderte Baustelle, und Familien lebten über Generationen daneben. Die Steinmetze, die anfingen, sahen das Dach nie. Die Kirche ist gotisch, ein Stil, der nach oben strebt, und sie misst 72 Meter bis zur Spitze. Benannt ist sie nach Anastasia von Rom.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Work began here in 1290, and the church was still going up in 1471. That is nearly two centuries of building, and families lived beside the site for generations. The masons who began it never saw the roof. It is Gothic, a style that reaches upward, and it stands 72 metres from the ground to the tip. The church is named for Anastasia of Rome.

localizedStory.de: Die hohe gotische Kirche von Verona, 72 Meter bis zur Spitze. 1290 begann der Bau, 1471 wurde noch daran gearbeitet.
localizedStory.en: Verona's tall Gothic church, 72 metres to the tip. Builders started in 1290 and were still at work in 1471.

fruits.name: Chiesa di Sant'Anastasia
fruits.story: Verona's tall Gothic church, 72 metres to the tip. Builders started in 1290 and were still at work in 1471.

fruits.extendedStory: Building started in 1117, and in 1187 Pope Urban III came to consecrate the finished church. It is Romanesque, which means round arches and thick, calm walls. The treasure inside is Titian's Pala dell'Assunta. French troops carried it off during the Napoleonic campaigns. It hangs in Verona again today, and no other work by Titian is in this city.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Bau begann 1117, und 1187 kam Papst Urban III. und weihte die fertige Kirche. Sie ist romanisch. Das bedeutet Rundbogen und dicke, ruhige Mauern. Der Schatz im Inneren ist Tizians Pala dell'Assunta. Französische Truppen schafften sie in den napoleonischen Feldzügen fort. Heute hängt sie wieder in Verona, und kein anderes Werk Tizians ist in dieser Stadt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Building started in 1117, and in 1187 Pope Urban III came to consecrate the finished church. It is Romanesque, which means round arches and thick, calm walls. The treasure inside is Titian's Pala dell'Assunta. French troops carried it off during the Napoleonic campaigns. It hangs in Verona again today, and no other work by Titian is in this city.

localizedStory.de: Der Dom wurde 1187 von Papst Urban III. geweiht. Drinnen hängt ein Gemälde von Tizian, das die Franzosen einst fortschafften.
localizedStory.en: The cathedral was consecrated in 1187 by Pope Urban III. Inside hangs a painting by Titian that the French once carried away.

fruits.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria Matricolare
fruits.story: The cathedral was consecrated in 1187 by Pope Urban III. Inside hangs a painting by Titian that the French once carried away.

fruits.extendedStory: The theatre was built towards the end of the 1st century BC. From the 10th century, houses and churches went up on its remains and covered the seating and stage completely. For hundreds of years there was nothing left to see. Then Andrea Monga, a merchant who lived from 1794 to 1861, bought the whole area and dug it out. In 1904 the city took the site over and carried the work on.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Theater entstand gegen Ende des 1. Jahrhunderts vor Christus. Ab dem 10. Jahrhundert wuchsen Häuser und Kirchen auf seinen Resten und deckten Zuschauerrund und Bühnenhaus vollständig zu. Jahrhundertelang war davon nichts mehr zu sehen. Dann kaufte Andrea Monga, ein Kaufmann, der von 1794 bis 1861 lebte, das ganze Gelände und grub es aus. 1904 übernahm die Stadt das Gelände und führte die Arbeit weiter.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The theatre was built towards the end of the 1st century BC. From the 10th century, houses and churches went up on its remains and covered the seating and stage completely. For hundreds of years there was nothing left to see. Then Andrea Monga, a merchant who lived from 1794 to 1861, bought the whole area and dug it out. In 1904 the city took the site over and carried the work on.

localizedStory.de: Ein römisches Theater, das verschwand. Ab dem 10. Jahrhundert wuchsen Häuser darüber, bis ein Kaufmann das ganze Gelände kaufte und es ausgrub.
localizedStory.en: A Roman theatre that vanished. Houses went up over it from the 10th century, until a merchant bought the whole area and dug it out.

fruits.name: Teatro Romano
fruits.story: A Roman theatre that vanished. Houses went up over it from the 10th century, until a merchant bought the whole area and dug it out.

fruits.extendedStory: Two powers wanted this hilltop. Across the 14th and 15th centuries the Castello Visconteo stood here, built for Gian Galeazzo Visconti as a fortified citadel. Later the Austrians raised a barracks to quarter their soldiers, and that long block still dominates the hill today. It stands 17.6 metres tall on a hill 118 metres high. From the top the whole old town lies below you.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Zwei Mächte wollten diesen Hügel. Im 14. und 15. Jahrhundert stand hier das Castello Visconteo, gebaut für Gian Galeazzo Visconti als befestigte Zitadelle. Später errichteten die Österreicher eine Kaserne für ihre Soldaten. Dieser lange Block beherrscht den Hügel bis heute. Er ist 17,6 Meter hoch und steht auf einem Hügel von 118 Metern. Von oben liegt die ganze Altstadt unter dir.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Two powers wanted this hilltop. Across the 14th and 15th centuries the Castello Visconteo stood here, built for Gian Galeazzo Visconti as a fortified citadel. Later the Austrians raised a barracks to quarter their soldiers, and that long block still dominates the hill today. It stands 17.6 metres tall on a hill 118 metres high. From the top the whole old town lies below you.

localizedStory.de: Der Hügel über dem Fluss, 118 Meter hoch. Das lange Gebäude oben ist eine Kaserne, die die Österreicher für ihre Soldaten bauten.
localizedStory.en: The hill above the river, 118 metres up. The long building on top is a barracks the Austrians built to quarter their soldiers.

fruits.name: Castel San Pietro
fruits.story: The hill above the river, 118 metres up. The long building on top is a barracks the Austrians built to quarter their soldiers.

fruits.extendedStory: The gate was built in the 1st century BC out of tuff, a soft volcanic stone, and brick. A hundred years later the Romans dressed it up. They set fronts of local white stone against the brick faces, so travellers arrived at something grand. The lions are not on the gate at all. The name has stuck since the 15th century, and comes from a Roman coffin nearby carved with two lions.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Tor entstand im 1. Jahrhundert vor Christus aus Tuff, einem weichen Vulkanstein, und aus Ziegeln. Hundert Jahre später schmückten es die Römer. Sie stellten Fronten aus hellem heimischem Stein vor die Ziegelfassaden. Die Löwen sitzen gar nicht am Tor. Der Name hält sich seit dem 15. Jahrhundert und stammt von einem römischen Sarg in der Nähe, in den zwei Löwen gemeißelt sind.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The gate was built in the 1st century BC out of tuff, a soft volcanic stone, and brick. A hundred years later the Romans dressed it up. They set fronts of local white stone against the brick faces, so travellers arrived at something grand. The lions are not on the gate at all. The name has stuck since the 15th century, and comes from a Roman coffin nearby carved with two lions.

localizedStory.de: Ein römisches Tor, das in einer Hauswand steckt. Benannt ist es nach zwei Löwen auf einem römischen Sarg aus der Nähe.
localizedStory.en: A Roman gate standing in a house wall on Via Leoni. It is named for two lions carved on a Roman coffin found nearby.

fruits.name: Porta Leoni
fruits.story: A Roman gate standing in a house wall on Via Leoni. It is named for two lions carved on a Roman coffin found nearby.
